**Data Processing Loop:**
```c


for (int i = tid * ELEMENTS_PER_THREAD; i < feature_dim; i += blockDim.x * ELEMENTS_PER_THREAD)
```

With 257 threads, thread 256 starts at element 2048 with a stride of 2056, while with 256 threads, thread 255 starts at 2040 with a stride of 2048. With 257 threads and stride 2056, thread 0 covers indices 0-7 then 2056-2063, thread 1 handles 8-15 then 2064-2071, and thread 254 processes 2032-2039 then 4088-4095. The original version with 256 threads splits the work differently—first iteration processes 0-2047, second handles 2048-4095—but also covers everything.

In the final reduction step, only warp 0 participates. Each lane reads from shared memory if its index is less than 8 (since 257 / 32 = 8 in integer division). So lanes 0-7 successfully load their corresponding values from shared_pos and shared_neg, while lanes 8-31 get zero values.

The original version with 256 threads has exactly 8 warps, so all partial sums are captured in the final read.
